Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

comentarios.texto: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: Claims the per-client resource lookup uses server.getId() as owner while resources are created with server.getClientId(), so client-specific permissions are never found.
issues.textoGolden: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

issues.descricao: Claims that with both fine-grained features enabled, client deletion calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled()/isPermissionsEnabled()/resource()/getPermissions() throw UnsupportedOperationException, but the provider listener registered in AdminPermissions.java:89-91 still calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client,false) on ClientRemovedEvent. WHY: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is not dependent on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (see Profile.java line 58), so when both FGAP features are enabled the guard at AdminPermissions.java:77 passes, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, clients() returns the throwing V2 evaluator, and every client deletion raises UnsupportedOperationException instead of cleaning up the client's permissions. HOW: either have the listener skip setPermissionsEnabled when the evaluator is the V2 implementation, or implement setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 to delete/ignore the per-client resource instead of throwing.

Under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ the listener now runs and the ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). management(...) returns MgmtPermissionsV2, which this PR changed to return ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Previously clients() returned the V1 ClientPermissions and this cleanup succeeded, so deleting a client with the feature enabled now fails with UnsupportedOperationException. Guard the call (e.g. only invoke it for non-V2 / feature-disabled evaluators) or give ClientPermissionsV2 a no-op setPermissionsEnabled so the removal event no longer throws.

With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). But MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Deleting a client therefore raises an unhandled exception inside the provider event listener (which carries its own KeycloakSession and runs inside the removal flow), breaking client removal. The listener must not invoke the V2 throwing stub — e.g. skip this cleanup for V2 or guard on the evaluator actually supporting it.

issues.descricao: Claims the all-clients resource lookup in hasPermission(String) cannot find the resource (owner mismatch or not lazily created), so global client permissions are ignored.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: hasPermission(String scope) resolves the all-clients resource with resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()), passing server.getId() as the ownerId, while the resource is created with owner server.getClientId() (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource line 104) and the default findByName(ResourceServer,String) overload uses server.getClientId(). WHY: if ResourceServer.getId() differs from ResourceServer.getClientId(), the lookup never matches, this method always returns null->false, and the global 'all clients' MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE permissions are silently ignored; the same 3-arg owner mismatch also appears in hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope) at line 214 (client.getId() with owner server.getId()). HOW: use the 2-arg findByName(server, name) (or pass server.getClientId() as ownerId) consistently with how the resource is created.

hasPermission(String scope) looks up the all-clients resource with findByName and returns false when it is null. That call is not guaranteed to find the resource, because it is created lazily through getResourceTypeResource, which the sibling hasPermission(client, scope) uses. As a result, canView(), canManage() and canManageClientScopes() can wrongly deny access when the all-clients resource has not been created yet. Fix: obtain the resource through AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), as the per-client variant does.

issues.descricao: Claims the client management-permissions endpoint returns a 500 under V2 because it calls ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException.

comentarios.texto: In V2, isPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions now throw UnsupportedOperationException. ClientResource (around lines 710-720) calls these on permissions.clients() with no V2 guard, so the management-permissions endpoint would return a 500 instead of a clean response when V2 is active. Return a safe value (for example isPermissionsEnabled returning false) or guard the callers.

issues.descricao: Claims hasPermission(client, scope) accepts permissions granted on other resources because it does not filter by resource id, allowing privilege escalation across clients.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) accepts any returned Permission whose scopes contain the expected scope without checking permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()), unlike UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission which filters by resource id. WHY: An evaluation result granting the scope on a different resource (other client or the all-clients resource when evaluating a per-client resource, or vice-versa) incorrectly authorizes the requested client — privilege escalation across clients. HOW: Filter results by resource id before matching scopes, as UserPermissionsV2 does.

issues.descricao: Claims getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every client resource, causing O(N) slowdowns.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getClientsWithPermission iterates every Clients resource via findByType and calls hasGrantedPermission->evaluatePermission separately for each resource. WHY: Listing/filtering clients triggers O(N) full policy evaluations where N is the number of client authorization resources, causing material slowdown and DB/policy-store fanout on realms with many clients. HOW: Batch-evaluate once or query granted resources via a single evaluation / indexed permission lookup instead of per-resource evaluation.

sugestoes.texto: GrafanaRuleListItem now supplies only promRule, but AlertRuleMenu still requires rulerRule to render Delete. Consequently, users with delete permission lose the Delete action throughout the new Grafana list. Update the delete menu and handler contract to use the existing identifier/groupIdentifier without requiring a loaded ruler rule.

The new Prometheus-only action props leave AlertRuleMenu's pause item gated by rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule), which is false when rulerRule is absent. Users can no longer pause or resume Grafana rules from the list despite the new ability hook granting Pause. Adapt the pause item to accept the Prometheus rule/identifier and obtain the mutation data when invoked.

RuleActionsButtons now accepts promRule without rule, but its silence drawer still mounts only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. Clicking the newly enabled Silence notifications item only sets showSilenceDrawer and displays nothing for Grafana list rows. Adapt the drawer to the Prometheus UID or load the ruler rule before mounting it.

useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously checked isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and marked Update/Delete unsupported for federated Mimir groups. Delegating here drops that group information, and useAllRulerRuleAbilities explicitly sets isFederated=false. Existing consumers of the CombinedRule hook therefore receive mutation abilities for federated rules whenever their datasource permissions allow editing/deleting, instead of the previous immutable result. Preserve the federated-group check in this wrapper or pass the group information into the delegated implementation.

AlertRuleMenu now passes skipToken for every non-Grafana rule and ORs the returned abilities with the ruler abilities. Converting skipToken to undefined does not disable this hook: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) sets MaybeSupported to AlwaysSupported once loading ends and grants Duplicate based on the user's Grafana rule-create permission. A user with that permission can consequently see Duplicate for a data-source rule even when its own ruler ability is unsupported or denied. Return [false, false] for every requested action when the input is skipToken (and apply the same behavior to the singular hook), while still calling the underlying hooks unconditionally.

issues.descricao: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based pause ability cannot display Pause or Resume for list-view rules because the menu still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) before rendering MenuItemPauseRule. GrafanaRuleListItem now supplies only promRule, so these actions disappear even for editable rules. Adapt the pause menu item to accept the Grafana identifier and Prometheus pause state, or load the ruler rule on demand.

issues.descricao: The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based delete ability is still gated by `canDelete && rulerRule` when rendering the Delete item. Both Grafana list-view paths now omit rulerRule, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action entirely. Render deletion using the available identifier and group identifier instead of requiring the ruler DTO, adapting the callback contract accordingly.

issues.descricao: When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: canDuplicate ORs ruler ability with grafana ability where grafana path is skipToken=>undefined for cloud rules, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) returns Duplicate=[true,true] whenever the user has global Grafana create permission. WHY: Any user with Grafana rule-create gets Duplicate menu item on cloud/Mimir rules even when ruler abilities deny it — incorrect authorization gating. HOW: Return NotSupported for all abilities when rule is skipToken/undefined, or gate grafana branch on prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) before ORing.

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns AlwaysSupported for Duplicate when rule is undefined (skipToken): loading is false from the !rule early-return, so MaybeSupported=true and duplicateSupported=true. ORed in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons this leaks Grafana create permission into non-Grafana rules. Gate MaybeSupported/duplicateSupported on rule existence (e.g. NotSupported when !rule).

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities must return NotSupported for all actions when rule is undefined (skipToken). Currently MaybeSupported falls back to AlwaysSupported when !loading, so Duplicate=[true, global-create] is true for a cloud rule passed as skipToken, and AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons OR-logic then incorrectly enables Duplicate (and Explore). Guard with if (!rule) return all-NotSupported abilities or make MaybeSupported require rule.

issues.descricao: The refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities into useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops the isFederatedRuleGroup check (isFederated is hardcoded false), so federated Mimir rules are reported as editable and deletable.

comentarios.texto: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false. The previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check is gone, so federated Mimir rules are no longer treated as immutable and can show edit and delete abilities. Keep the federation check in this wrapper, or pass the federation state into the shared hook.

Delegating useAllAlertRuleAbilities to useAllRulerRuleAbilities discards the group's federation status and replaces the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check with a constant false. Legacy RuleActionsButtons consequently enables editing rules in groups with source_tenants, although these groups were explicitly immutable before this change. Preserve the CombinedRule federation check in the wrapper or pass federation status into the delegated ability calculation.

Preserve the federated-group immutability check when delegating this CombinedRule hook. Previously useAllAlertRuleAbilities inspected rule.group with isFederatedRuleGroup and disabled modification/removal for federated rules. The replacement delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated=false and receives no group information. Existing useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities consumers therefore now receive supported update/delete abilities for federated rules when datasource permissions allow them, exposing operations that the previous contract explicitly prohibited. Pass the federation state through or retain that restriction in this wrapper.

issues.descricao: The Grafana prom-rule abilities gate Pause, Restore, Export and DeletePermanently on alertingRule(rule) while the comment claims it checks Grafana-managed rules, so Grafana recording rules lose these actions in the list view.

comentarios.texto: The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the variable it describes is `isAlertingRule`. That variable is true only for alerting rules and false for Grafana recording rules. Fix the comment, or rename the variable, so it says the check is for alerting rules. As written, readers will expect Pause, Export and Silence to be enabled for recording rules.

The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the check used is alertingRule(rule), which is false for recording rules. Pause, Restore, ModifyExport and DeletePermanently are therefore wrongly disabled for Grafana recording rules, where the old isGrafanaManagedAlertRule check allowed them. Use prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) for these abilities, and keep alertingRule only for Silence.

issues.descricao: The comment claims GrafanaPromRuleDTO abilities have no loading state, but the next line makes support depend on the folder loading flag.

comentarios.texto: The comment says there is no loading state, but the next line is `loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`. `loading` comes from the folder fetch. Update the comment to say that support depends on the folder loading state.

issues.descricao: The Grafana branch of the filtered rule list renders GrafanaRuleListItem without a key prop, so React reconciles the streaming list by index and warns about missing keys.
issues.textoGolden: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The grafana branch of the filtered list renders <GrafanaRuleListItem .../> without a `key` prop, dropping the `key={key}` that the replaced <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../> had. WHY: `rules.map` renders a dynamic list keyed by getRuleKey/hashRule; without a key React logs duplicate-key warnings and reconciles rows by index, so as the async rule stream updates/reorders the wrong rule row can be reused/mutated (stale state, swapped actions). HOW: add `key={key}` (the value is already destructured on line 152) to the <GrafanaRuleListItem> element.

WHAT: Grafana branch of FilterViewResults renders GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key} while datasource and unknown branches pass key. WHY: Breaks React list reconciliation — wrong item reuse, stale actions/state and console key warnings for every Grafana hit. HOW: Add key={key} to the GrafanaRuleListItem element.

issues.descricao: The test named 'should render More button with action menu options' only checks the More button exists, never the menu options.

comentarios.texto: The test 'should render More button with action menu options' only checks that the More button exists. It finds the button by name 'More', so the aria-label and text assertions are tautological. It would pass even if the menu had no actions or the abilities were broken. Click the button and assert the expected menu items, or rename the test to match what it checks.

Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' never verifies any action menu option: the body only asserts the More button exists and has aria-label/text 'More'. It would still pass if the dropdown were rendered empty (Silence/Duplicate/Copy link/Export all missing), i.e. the behaviour the name promises is not covered. Either open the menu and assert the menu items, or rename the test to reflect that it only checks the trigger button's rendering/accessibility.

Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' never opens the menu nor asserts menu items — it only checks More button presence/aria/text. Click More and assert expected menuitems (or rename to 'should render More button') so it fails if menu actions break.

issues.descricao: GrafanaGroupLoader's JSDoc still says it loads from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints after the ruler query was removed.

comentarios.texto: The JSDoc for GrafanaGroupLoader still says "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints." but this PR removed the ruler API query entirely — the component now only calls useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery (Prometheus). The documentation describes a data source the function no longer consumes; update it to state only the Prometheus endpoint is loaded (and the same stale "Ruler response" reference in the expectedRulesCount prop doc at lines 18–19 should be corrected).

issues.descricao: For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.
issues.textoGolden: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

comentarios.texto: Passing only promRule enables the Silence notifications menu item but leaves RuleActionsButtons.V2 unable to render its silence drawer, which is guarded by rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). Clicking Silence only updates showSilenceDrawer and displays nothing because rule is undefined. Update the drawer to accept a rule UID—the inspected SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only needs grafana_alert.uid—and allow the Prometheus alerting-rule path to render it.

The new list item passes only promRule to RuleActionsButtons, but that component renders SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only under `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. With rule undefined, clicking the newly enabled 'Silence notifications' action only sets state and never opens a drawer. Adapt the silence rendering path to load/use the rule by its Prometheus identifier before switching this caller to promRule-only.

WHAT: getEditableIdentifier now enables a prom-only path (Grafana uid identifier with rulerRule undefined) but the silence drawer still renders only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. WHY: In the list view Silence menu item can be shown via grafana abilities, clicking it sets showSilenceDrawer but the drawer never mounts, so Silence silently does nothing. HOW: Gate the drawer on promRule as well or provide a prom-based silence drawer.

issues.descricao: Claims provisioned status now comes from promRule.provenance, which the Prometheus response might omit, making provisioned rules editable.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: isProvisioned derived from promRule.provenance (new optional field) instead of ruler grafana_alert.provenance. WHY: If the Prometheus groups response omits provenance, provisioned rules render as non-provisioned and abilities (isProvisionedPromRule) fail open to editable/removable. HOW: Ensure Prometheus API populates provenance or fall back to ruler/folder metadata for the provisioned check.

issues.descricao: Claims the promRule prop typed as Rule makes the Grafana prom-rule type guard return false for the GrafanaPromRuleDTO passed by GrafanaRuleListItem.

comentarios.texto: The `promRule` prop is declared as `Rule` (the combined-rule type from app/types/unified-alerting, the same type used for `useRulePluginLinkExtension`), but the body consumes it as a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`: it feeds it to `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken` -> `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(rule: GrafanaPromRuleDTO | SkipToken, …)` and to `isProvisionedPromRule(promRule: PromRuleDTO)`. The new producer GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx passes a raw GrafanaPromRuleDTO into this `Rule`-typed slot. Because `Rule` is not a prom-rule DTO, the type guard returns false for combined-rule callers (e.g. the RulesTable path) so the Grafana abilities resolve to NotSupported and the new menu entries are silently hidden, while the list-view caller only appears to work by passing a differently-typed object. Align the prop type with what the hooks/guards require (GrafanaPromRuleDTO) on the side the caller must satisfy, and update GrafanaRuleListItem accordingly.

sugestoes.texto: The async forEach callback turns getCalendar failures into rejected promises that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch. Invalid encrypted CalDAV/Apple credentials can throw during service construction (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts decrypts and JSON-parses the key), so rescheduling now produces an unhandled rejection instead of logging the error and continuing; the same regression appears in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Await Promise.all over mapped callbacks inside the try block, or use an awaited for...of loop, in both implementations.

The enclosing forEach does not await its async callbacks. Previously getCalendar returned synchronously, so callbacks could populate apiDeletes before yielding; this new await yields before any calendar operations are queued. The handler can consequently await the current apiDeletes array and finish without waiting for recurring calendar updates/deletions, allowing failures to escape the cancellation flow and work to be lost when the request ends. Await the credential callbacks (for example with Promise.all over map), or use an awaited for...of loop, before consuming apiDeletes.

This async forEach is not awaited. Adding await getCalendar here means each callback now suspends before it can register the recurring-event operations in apiDeletes. The handler can reach its Promise.all(apiDeletes) and finish cancellation before those operations have been added, leaving external recurring events stale (and subsequent failures outside the handler's awaited work). Await the iteration itself, for example with an awaited Promise.all over map, before consuming apiDeletes.

issues.descricao: Async callbacks passed to forEach after getCalendar became async are never awaited, so calendar and video cancellations run fire-and-forget, may not finish, and their errors escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections.
issues.textoGolden: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

comentarios.texto: The async forEach callback moves calendar factory exceptions outside the surrounding try/catch because forEach discards its returned promise. An invalid encrypted Exchange credential throws during CalendarService construction, now producing an unhandled rejection while Reschedule continues and returns success instead of logging the error; the identical regression occurs in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Await Promise.all over bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...) inside the try block, or use an awaited for...of loop, so factory and deletion failures reach the catch.

The new async forEach callback is not awaited. If getCalendar rejects (for example, the dynamically imported calendar module fails to load or its service constructor throws), the callback produces a rejected promise that forEach discards; the surrounding try/catch cannot catch it. Previously a synchronous getCalendar failure reached that catch. Await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) or use an awaited for...of loop so these failures remain handled and calendar cleanup completes before rescheduling continues. Apply the same fix to the equivalent changed loop in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

WHAT: credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar; apiDeletes.push(...) }) pushes to apiDeletes asynchronously after outer code consumes it. WHY: outer apiDeletes is awaited elsewhere while async callbacks have not yet pushed, so recurring-event deletions are lost/partial and errors are unobserved. HOW: replace with for...of with await or collect promises via map + await Promise.all.

issues.descricao: Suggests wrapping the awaited dynamic app import in try-catch to handle import failures, without identifying a defect.
issues.textoGolden: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

issues.descricao: Claims consumers of getCalendarCredentials call methods on or null-check an un-awaited Promise; every consumer goes through getConnectedCalendars, which awaits it.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getCalendar changed to async Promise<Calendar|null> but packages/core/CalendarManager.ts getCalendarCredentials still does const calendar = getCalendar(credential) synchronously without await. WHY: every entry now stores a Promise instead of Calendar, so any consumer not patched to await item.calendar (e.g. callers in viewer.tsx/calendar.ts paths) sees a truthy Promise, breaks null checks and calls listCalendars/createEvent on wrong type. HOW: make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar, updating its callers.

getCalendar is now async but getCalendarCredentials still does `const calendar = getCalendar(credential)` without await in a sync function, so `calendar` is a Promise. Make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar (update callers) so its contract again returns Calendar|null.

getCalendar now returns a Promise, so getCalendarCredentials returns items whose `calendar` field is a Promise<Calendar|null>, not a Calendar. Only getConnectedCalendars awaits it. Other consumers (apps/web/pages/api/availability/calendar.ts and trpc viewer.tsx) that use `.calendar` directly would call methods on a Promise. Make getCalendarCredentials async and await getCalendar, or update every consumer to await `.calendar`.

issues.descricao: Claims the import() calls in the appStore object load every app eagerly and should be thunks; the asynchronous loading works as intended.

comentarios.texto: Each `import("./app")` in the object literal runs when the module is first imported, so all apps still load eagerly and nothing is lazy. A module that fails to load also produces an unhandled rejection if nobody awaits that entry. Store thunks instead, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and have callers do `await appStore[key]?.()`.

issues.descricao: The commented example entry in app-store/index.ts points to ./example instead of ./_example.

comentarios.texto: The comment/example line names a module path that does not exist: the example app lives at `packages/app-store/_example`, but the comment is written as `// example: import("./example"),` (the previous line referenced `"./_example"`). Because this comment is the copy-paste instruction for re-enabling the example app, uncommenting it verbatim fails to resolve `./example`. Point the path back at `./_example` so the prose matches the actual directory.

issues.descricao: Claims getVideoAdapters performs N sequential module-load round trips per request; the imports already started in parallel at module load.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getVideoAdapters awaits each dynamic appStore import sequentially in for...of. WHY: availability/meeting paths now pay N sequential module-load round-trips per request instead of one parallel fan-out, adding latency on hot getAvailability/createMeeting calls with multiple credentials. HOW: collect promises then await Promise.all, e.g. Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...)).

sugestoes.texto: The exported Prometheus help text says this histogram measures request sizes "returned", but QueryData observes len(v.JSON) from the incoming queries and CallResource observes len(req.Body). No response size is measured. This misleads operators interpreting the metric as returned payload volume; describe it as incoming plugin request sizes instead.

Both size-instrumented cases send empty payloads, and checkHistogram only verifies a nonzero sample count, not the observed size. Consequently, replacing the size calculations in QueryData and CallResource with a constant zero leaves this test green even though request-size instrumentation is broken. Supply nonempty query JSON and resource bodies and assert the size histogram's sample sum equals their expected byte lengths.

Both observation paths convert to float64 only after integer duration division. A 900µs plugin request is therefore recorded as 0ms, and a 1.9ms request as 1ms. This materially distorts the explicitly configured sub-millisecond histogram buckets and undercounts latency relative to the seconds metric. Divide floating-point durations in both paths instead.

issues.descricao: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh TestLogger instead of the receiver, so logs written via the contextual logger are lost to assertions on the original fake.
issues.textoGolden: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger instead of the receiver. WHY: LoggerMiddleware calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info so the write goes to a throwaway instance and assertions on the original TestLogger Calls/Message never observe it, diverging from real wrapper that preserves logger context. HOW: Return f (or a child sharing f) instead of NewTestLogger.

issues.descricao: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after the middleware was renamed to MetricsMiddleware.

comentarios.texto: TestInstrumentationMiddleware still carries the old name even though this PR renamed the middleware under test to MetricsMiddleware (newMetricsMiddleware/NewMetricsMiddleware) and the file to metrics_middleware_test.go. The identifier advertises the superseded "InstrumentationMiddleware" name; rename it (e.g. TestMetricsMiddleware) so the test name matches the code it exercises.
Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware but it constructs and asserts MetricsMiddleware (newMetricsMiddleware). Rename to TestMetricsMiddleware to match the renamed middleware.

issues.descricao: Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil requests because it reads req.PluginContext without a nil guard.
issues.textoGolden: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics dereference req (req.PluginContext) without nil guard. WHY: Sibling LoggerMiddleware in same PR added explicit if req==nil guards, and direct middleware invocation with nil panics; inconsistent contract. HOW: Add same if req==nil passthrough guard before instrumentContext.

QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics dereference req (req.Queries, req.Body, req.PluginContext) without the `if req == nil` guard that LoggerMiddleware uses. A nil request panics. Add nil guards forwarding to next like LoggerMiddleware does.

QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics read req.PluginContext without checking req == nil. A nil request panics before LoggerMiddleware's guard. Add `if req == nil { return m.next.<Method>(ctx, req, ...) }` guards.

issues.descricao: Claims the refactor dropped traceID from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines.
issues.textoGolden: The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

comentarios.texto: LoggerMiddleware (logger_middleware.go:58) now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx) and relies on the context for all per-request attributes, but the middleware that replaced its enrichment (instrumentContext) re-adds only endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname. The traceID that logger_middleware.go previously appended itself (via tracing.TraceIDFromContext) is never put into the contextual logger, so the 'Plugin Request Completed'/grafana-data-egress line loses its traceID and log-trace correlation silently breaks. Add the trace id to the contextual attributes here (e.g. append 'traceID', tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) when non-empty) so the consumer's assumption holds.

The migration to the contextual logger dropped the traceID field. Before this PR, logRequest explicitly appended "traceID" (from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)) to logParams. The change moved pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID into the context (ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext) and logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx), but instrumentContext does NOT add traceID. Result: "Plugin Request Completed" egress log lines silently lose their traceID, breaking correlation between plugin request logs and traces. Fix by having instrumentContext (or the logParams here) also carry the trace ID, e.g. append "traceID", tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) in instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go, or re-add it to logParams here.

The traceID key was dropped from logParams (along with the pkg/infra/tracing import) and is now expected to come from m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The only thing that populates that context is the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext, which adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname but never traceID. The metrics middleware in this same PR still has to read the trace ID explicitly (metrics_middleware.go:127), confirming it is not supplied by the logger itself. Restore an explicit "traceID", tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) entry in logParams, or have instrumentContext add the trace ID, otherwise 'Plugin Request Completed' logs lose trace correlation.

issues.descricao: Claims the metrics middleware factory mutates a shared instance's next field, causing a data race between chains.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware captures a single shared *MetricsMiddleware (`imw`) and mutates `imw.next = next` inside the middleware factory, which is re-invoked on every request because Decorator rebuilds the chain per call. WHY: concurrent requests write/read `imw.next` without synchronization, causing a data race (flagged by -race) and the possibility that a request dispatches into another request's inner chain. HOW: build a fresh instance per chain, e.g. `return plugins.ClientMiddlewareFunc(func(next plugins.Client) plugins.Client { return &MetricsMiddleware{pluginMetrics: imw.pluginMetrics, pluginRegistry: imw.pluginRegistry, next: next} })`.

WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware reuses a single shared MetricsMiddleware instance and mutates imw.next on every CreateClientMiddleware call. WHY: Concurrent or multiple Decorator chains overwrite next on the same object causing data race and requests routed to the wrong next client, unlike Contextual/Logger middlewares that allocate per chain. HOW: Allocate a new MetricsMiddleware per chain (copy metrics handles, set next) instead of mutating the shared imw.

issues.descricao: Claims the request-size histogram's HELP text says 'returned' though it measures request sizes.

comentarios.texto: The HELP text for grafana_plugin_request_size_bytes says "histogram of plugin request sizes returned", but the metric only measures the request sent to the plugin: QueryData sums len(v.JSON) over the outgoing queries (lines 145-148) and CallResource passes len(req.Body) (line 161). Nothing "returned" by the plugin is observed. This HELP string is surfaced to users in Prometheus/Grafana metric descriptions, so it documents the opposite of the recorded value; it should describe the plugin request (egress) size, not a response size.

The metric help text describes sizes "returned", but the observations measure incoming payloads: QueryData sums len(v.JSON) and CallResource uses len(req.Body), both before invoking the plugin. This description exposes request sizes as though they were response sizes to operators reading Prometheus metadata. Change the help text to describe incoming plugin request payload sizes.

issues.descricao: Claims the test never asserts that request size is not instrumented for CheckHealth/CollectMetrics.

comentarios.texto: The request-size assertion is entirely gated behind `if tc.shouldInstrumentRequestSize`, so the `shouldInstrumentRequestSize: false` cases (CheckHealth at line 45, CollectMetrics at line 68) verify nothing about request-size instrumentation. The case names claim request size must NOT be instrumented for those endpoints, yet the body makes no assertion for them. If a regression made CheckHealth/CollectMetrics call instrumentPluginRequestSize, CollectAndCount(metricRequestSize) would become 1 and this test would still pass. Add a negative assertion for the false cases, e.g. `require.Equal(t, 0, testutil.CollectAndCount(promRegistry, metricRequestSize))`.

The shouldInstrumentRequestSize=false cases (CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) never assert that the request size metric is absent. If size instrumentation were wrongly added to those endpoints, the test would still pass. Add an else branch that requires testutil.CollectAndCount(promRegistry, metricRequestSize) to equal 0.

Missing negative assertion: when shouldInstrumentRequestSize is false (CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) the test asserts nothing about grafana_plugin_request_size_bytes. If instrumentPluginRequestSize were incorrectly called for those endpoints, CollectAndCount would be 1 yet the test would still pass. Add else branch asserting CollectAndCount==0 / histogram absent.

issues.descricao: Claims checkHistogram carries foundLabels across metrics and returns errors prematurely.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: in checkHistogram, `foundLabels` is declared before the `for _, m := range metricFamily.Metric` loop and is never reset between metrics. WHY: the counter accumulates across metrics, so the `foundLabels != len(expLabels)` check is evaluated against a stale/inflated count — a metric with only a partial label match can be accepted (false pass) and a valid metric after a partial match can error (false fail), letting the metric assertions miss real regressions. HOW: move `foundLabels := 0` inside the outer loop (reset per metric).

`foundLabels` is declared outside the `for _, m := range metricFamily.Metric` loop and never reset per metric, and the code returns an error as soon as a metric has a matching label key with a different value (rather than `continue`-ing). The correct-metric decision therefore relies on state carried over between metrics and on a premature error return instead of an exact per-metric label comparison. With more than one series in a family this produces false failures and wrong "expected N labels, got M" counts. Reset the counter per metric and `continue` to the next metric when the label set does not fully match, instead of returning an error.

issues.descricao: Claims millisecond durations are truncated by integer division before conversion to float.

comentarios.texto: The millisecond observations truncate the duration before converting it to float64: elapsed/time.Millisecond is integer division. For example, a 900µs request is recorded as 0ms and a 1.9ms request as 1ms, misclassifying observations against the fractional millisecond buckets declared above and understating the histogram sum. Use float64(elapsed)/float64(time.Millisecond) in both the exemplar and ordinary observation paths to preserve the actual duration.

Incorrect measurement: float64(elapsed/time.Millisecond) and float64(elapsed / time.Millisecond) do integer division before conversion, truncating all sub-millisecond durations to 0. Buckets start at 0.005ms so precision matters. Use float64(elapsed)/float64(time.Millisecond).

issues.descricao: Claims the request-size test cases use empty payloads and would not detect a broken size calculation.

comentarios.texto: The request-size cases pass an empty Body and no Queries, and subsequently check only that a histogram sample exists. Replacing either size calculation with a constant zero still passes this test. Use nonempty resource bodies and query JSON payloads and assert the histogram sample sum equals their expected byte count, so broken request-size instrumentation is detected.

issues.descricao: Claims the duration metric checks only labels and sample counts, not the observed values.

comentarios.texto: Both duration metrics are checked only for labels and a nonzero sample count. Observing a constant zero, or feeding seconds into the milliseconds metric, still passes. Assert the observed durations using a controlled elapsed interval (or check the relationship between the two histogram sums with allowance for millisecond truncation) so the test detects broken duration values and units.

issues.descricao: Claims the duration-seconds histogram check omits status and source labels.

comentarios.texto: Assertion too loose for duration-seconds: plugin_request_duration_seconds has labels source,plugin_id,endpoint,status,target but checkHistogram is called with only plugin_id,endpoint,target. A broken status or source label (e.g. wrong status mapping) would still pass. Require all 5 labels including status==statusOK and source==grafana-backend, and verify observed size values not just sample count.

issues.descricao: Claims LoggerMiddleware depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running first and would log without plugin identity if reordered.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: logRequest dropped explicit pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID params and now relies solely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) populated by upstream ContextualLoggerMiddleware. WHY: Creates hidden ordering dependency (requires Contextual before Logger in pluginsintegration.go:160-161); standalone/reordered use silently logs without plugin identity. HOW: Keep explicit fallback from req.PluginContext/tracing when ctx has no attributes, or document/enforce ordering.

issues.descricao: Claims the metrics middleware now fails the request when the plugin is not in the registry.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: QueryData (and CallResource:161) abort the plugin call and return ErrPluginNotRegistered when instrumentPluginRequestSize/pluginTarget lookup fails. WHY: A best-effort observability lookup failure becomes a request failure, blocking the real plugin call that might have returned its own error. HOW: Log the target-lookup failure and continue to instrumentPluginRequest/next call instead of returning early.

Best-effort metrics now fails the request: QueryData (and CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics via the same helpers) returns ErrPluginNotRegistered from pluginTarget/instrumentPluginRequestSize without calling next when the plugin is missing from the registry. Callers lose the previous contract that instrumentation never refuses the request. Fix: do not propagate registry miss as request error — default target to unknown/skip observation and always invoke next.

sugestoes.texto: Fallback locales are preloaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths with unloaded fallback dictionaries. Jobs::Base sets the site locale and executes jobs without this filter, and post_alerter switches to a user's locale with I18n.with_locale; the accelerator loads only the active locale, while backend fallback lookups bypass that loader, so missing keys return missing translations instead of falling back to English or the site language in a fresh worker. Ensure the fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary rather than exclusively at the HTTP request boundary.

issues.descricao: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

issues.descricao: Claims a fallback value cached for a not-yet-loaded locale stays stale after that locale's file is loaded, because ensure_loaded! does not invalidate the translation cache.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new ensure_loaded! loads fallback locale files but does not invalidate the accelerator's shared @cache (only reload! clears it on lines 39-43), while the initializer now enables I18n::Backend::Fallbacks so a lookup for a not-yet-loaded locale returns the :en/default value instead of raising MissingTranslation. WHY: That fallback value is cached by translate under the requested locale key (line 72-76); when ensure_loaded!/load_locale later loads the correct locale file (e.g. a background job at app/jobs/base.rb:151 sets I18n.locale and translates before the locale is loaded, then a web request loads it), the stale fallback string is still served from cache for that locale. HOW: clear @cache when newly loading a locale (e.g. set `@cache = nil` inside load_locale/ensure_loaded! after adding a locale to @loaded_locales, or include the loaded-locale state in the cache key).

issues.descricao: Suggests normalizing the locale because a String locale mixed with Symbol fallback entries defeats uniq and causes double lookups or double loading.
issues.textoGolden: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] mixes types — the incoming `locale` is left as-is (a String, since I18n.locale is set to User#effective_locale / SiteSetting.default_locale which are Strings) while the other two chain entries are Symbols (`SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`, `:en`), so `.uniq` cannot deduplicate the current locale and returns e.g. ["en", :en]. WHY: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate/#exists? iterate this array and call super for every entry, so the current locale is looked up a second time on each cache miss, and FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded! calls I18n.ensure_loaded! for both "en" and :en, making load_locale parse and merge the same .yml file twice on the first request. HOW: normalize the argument first, e.g. `locale = locale.to_sym` at the top of `[]` (or build `[locale.to_sym, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`).

issues.descricao: Claims a nil default_locale makes FallbackLocaleList#[] raise NoMethodError on every missing translation.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym before uniq.compact, so a nil/missing default_locale raises NoMethodError. WHY: crashes fallback resolution (every missing key) during boot, DB-down, or unset setting instead of falling back to :en. HOW: guard nil e.g. SiteSetting.default_locale.try(:to_sym) before building the chain.

issues.descricao: Claims every fallback lookup hits the database or Redis through SiteSetting.default_locale, amplifying per-request load.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] queries SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallbacks[locale] lookup. WHY: with fallbacks enabled every missing translation triggers a SiteSetting (DB/Redis) hit in the translate hot path, amplifying per-request query/load cost. HOW: memoize/cache the default-locale segment and invalidate only when the setting changes.

issues.descricao: Claims a user-controlled locale with regex metacharacters reaches load_locale's Regexp and forces loading of unintended locale files.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: New I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale) forwards the locale unchecked into load_locale which builds Regexp.new("\\.#{locale}\\.yml$") for load_path.grep. WHY: the locale chain includes user-controlled I18n.locale (current_user.effective_locale via FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!), so regex metacharacters (e.g. .* ) widen the match and force loading of unintended/all locale files (resource exhaustion / unexpected translation loading). HOW: escape the locale with Regexp.escape and/or validate against LocaleSiteSetting.supported_locales before loading.

issues.descricao: Claims @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and shared across threads without synchronization.
issues.textoGolden: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
